extracted.intended_audience: members of the District of Columbia Bar, Bar leadership (Board of Governors, Executive Committee), and D.C. Court of Appeals
extracted.subtask_short: D.C. Bar bylaws and membership rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official bylaws and accompanying explanatory text setting membership classes and requirements, governance structure and duties of the Board and Executive Committee, meeting and voting rules, officer qualifications, and related procedural standards for the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Manual authority and amendment process
rubrics_metrics.description: The D.C. Bar Membership Manual shall have the same weight and authority of these Bylaws. The provisions and requirements contained in the Membership Manual may not be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Membership Manual shall be amended upon the recommendation of the Chief Executive Officer and shall take effect unless the Executive Committee raises a written objection to the recommendation no later than two weeks after receiving written notice of such amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active membership (definition and rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active members are eligible to engage in the practice of law in the District of Columbia. Active members are eligible to hold office and vote in any election or other business conducted by the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactive membership (definition and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inactive members are those eligible for Active membership but who are not engaged in the practice of law in the District of Columbia and who have provided notice to the Bar of enrollment in this class of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as authorized by other Court rules, Inactive members shall not practice law in the District of Columbia and shall not be eligible to hold office or vote in any general election or other business conducted by the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial membership (definition and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial members include judges of courts of record, full-time court commissioners, U.S. bankruptcy judges, U.S. magistrate judges, other persons who perform a judicial function on an exclusive basis in an official capacity, and retired judges eligible for temporary judicial assignment, who are not engaged in the practice of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial members shall not be eligible to practice law in the District of Columbia or to hold office or vote in any general election or vote on other business conducted by the District of Columbia Bar. If employment terms require eligibility to practice, member may choose to be Active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired membership (definition and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired members are persons who have retired from the practice of law (except pro bono as provided in D.C. App R. 49), or who are totally disabled and unable to practice law, and who have certified (1) five years of Active membership (with substitution rules for Inactive/Judicial), and (2) a total of 25 years engaged in the practice of law in D.C. or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retired members shall not be eligible to hold office or vote in any general election or other business conducted by the District of Columbia Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Legal Consultants category
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Legal Consultants licensed by the Court are not members of the Bar but are subject to the same conditions and requirements under the applicable Rules, Bylaws, and Membership Manual as Active members of the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These persons may render legal services in D.C. as permitted by Court rules, are subject to specific limitations, are exempt from the Mandatory Course requirement, and shall not be eligible to hold office or vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to create additional membership classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall have the authority to create additional classes of membership and promulgate the required qualifications for such classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual registration and change of information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: On or before July 1st, all Active, Inactive, and Judicial members must file annually a registration statement in electronic form as required by the Bar. All members must file changes to previously submitted registration information within 30 days of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly admitted members must file within three months of admission as authorized by the Court. Failure to timely submit changes may result in automatic administrative suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to register
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member who fails to file the required registration statement shall be suspended from membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended members shall not engage in the practice of law in the District of Columbia until they complete the reinstatement requirements set forth in the Membership Manual or unless otherwise authorized by D.C. App. R. 49.

rubrics_metrics.name: License fee and late fee
rubrics_metrics.description: All Active, Inactive, and Judicial members (and Special Legal Consultants) shall pay an annual license fee to remain in good standing. License fees shall be determined and approved by the Board of Governors and shall not exceed a ceiling set by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All license fees are due on or before July 1st (unless otherwise published). Fees are non-refundable once remitted. Members whose fees are not received by July 15th will be assessed and required to pay a late fee in addition to the full annual license fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to assess reinstatement fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall have the authority to assess and collect reinstatement fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension for nonpayment of license fee and/or late fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member whose annual license fee and/or assessed fees remain unpaid by September 30th shall be automatically administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as otherwise provided in D.C. App. R. 49, administratively suspended members shall not be entitled to practice law in the District of Columbia during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Course requirement for new admittees
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys admitted after July 1, 1994 are required to complete the Mandatory Course on the D.C. Rules of Professional Conduct and D.C. Practice within twelve months of admission to the Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly admitted attorneys who have not completed the Course within twelve months shall be sent a notice of noncompliance to their preferred Bar email address. Those not completing the Course within 60 days of issuance of the 12-month notice shall be automatically suspended and sent a Notice of Suspension to their preferred email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report on Mandatory Course
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bar shall provide a written report annually to the Court concerning the Course, its curriculum and faculty, number of presentations, attendance, and the number of attorneys suspended for failure to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in membership class, resignation, and reinstatement process location
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for change in membership class, resignation, and reinstatement are addressed fully in the Membership Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO discretion over membership status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Executive Officer may, in their discretion, authorize a change to a member’s official record or require other action be taken, including retroactive reinstatement, to address an error or omission by the Bar or upon other good cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions may be taken upon such terms and conditions the CEO deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices from the Bar to members and to courts; deadlines rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices shall be sent to the member’s preferred email address in their official Bar record. Notices of administrative suspension shall be sent in writing by first class U.S. mail and by email. The Bar shall provide written notice to the clerks of the D.C. Court of Appeals and/or the D.C. Superior Court of any suspensions arising under this Article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deadline that falls on a weekend or D.C. holiday shall be the next regular business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual membership meeting (time/place/notice/minutes/format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year there shall be an annual meeting of members. The Board of Governors shall determine the time and place and arrange a suitable program. The Annual Meeting shall be held in-person, electronically, or both, provided all attendees can contemporaneously communicate with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes of the Annual Meeting shall be approved by the Board. Notice of time and place must be provided to each Active member or published in an official Bar publication at least 30 days prior to the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special meetings of the membership (calling, petition, notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special meetings may be called by the Board of Governors or the President. The Secretary shall call a special meeting upon receipt of a petition signed by not less than three percent of Active members specifying the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petition meetings must be convened as promptly as possible and not later than 30 days after the Secretary receives the petition. Notice of time, place and purpose must be provided to each Active member or published at least 10 days prior to the meeting. The census of Active members shall be determined as of the first business day of the calendar year in which the petition is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and voting rules for membership meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred Active members present at any annual or special meeting shall constitute a quorum. No member shall be entitled to be represented by proxy. Only Active members in attendance at the time a vote is taken may participate in any vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action by a majority of the members present and voting shall constitute action by the membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Governors shall consist of no more than 23 members: (a) Twenty Active D.C. Bar members, including the Officers, the Immediate Past-President, and the Treasurer-Elect, all of whom shall be voting members; and (b) Three non-voting members who shall not have been admitted to practice law in any jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board terms and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All voting and non-voting members of the Board shall serve a three-year term beginning at the start of the fiscal year. Board members may not be elected to and may not serve more than two consecutive three-year terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board duties (general charge and specific authorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall have general charge of the affairs and activities of the Bar and shall have the authority to: (a) evaluate whether members' needs are being met; (b) develop a long-range strategic plan and measure progress; (c) request, receive, consider and take action on reports and recommendations; (d) ensure accurate financial reporting, approve the annual budget, monitor financial condition, and review outside audit; (e) fix time/place of annual meeting; (f) arrange for publication of an official Bar bulletin or journal; (g) conduct investigations of matters affecting the Bar; (h) authorize, when appropriate, public statements on major issues; (i) adopt Bylaws and regulations not inconsistent with the Rules; and (j) appoint, support, and evaluate the Chief Executive Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions (a), (b), and (j) align with best practices to set forth the Board's duties regarding members, strategy, and relationship with staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacancy-filling for Board seats
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a vacancy of a voting member (excluding President, President-Elect, Treasurer, Treasurer-Elect), the position shall be filled by the Board candidate receiving the next highest number of votes in the most recent regular annual election, subject to Board approval. If that candidate is unable or not approved, continue down the list to the next highest vote recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If process still results in a vacancy, or for a vacancy of a non-voting member, the President, in consultation with the CEO and Chair of the Committee on Nominations, shall appoint an individual to fill the position, subject to Board approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board regular meetings (frequency, scheduling, notice, agenda additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall hold up to eight regular meetings per fiscal year. Dates and locations shall be announced no later than June 30 of the prior fiscal year. The Board may change date/location for good cause without required notice to membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable written notice of time, place, and technology platform shall be provided to Board members, required Committee Chairs, Office of Disciplinary Counsel, Board on Professional Responsibility, and presidents of voluntary bar associations invited to attend. Any transactional business may be conducted at a regular meeting whether specified in the notice or not provided two-thirds of voting members present and voting approve adding the matter to the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board special meetings (calling and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special meetings may be called by the President, the Executive Committee, or five voting members of the Board. Reasonable written notice of time, place, technology platform, and subjects to be covered shall be provided to all members of the Board and required parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any transactional business within the Board's power may be conducted during a special meeting whether specified in the notice or not provided two-thirds of voting members present and voting approve the addition to the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic meetings and electronic attendance for Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Board meetings may be held in person or electronically, as long as all attendees can simultaneously hear each other and participate during the meeting. The President, the Board, or the Executive Committee shall determine whether to hold a meeting electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board members may, subject to the President's discretion, participate in an in-person meeting electronically or by other means by which all attendees can simultaneously hear each other and participate during the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of the voting members of the Board shall constitute a quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board voting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be no proxy voting allowed. Voting members of the Board must be in attendance, in person or electronically, at the meeting at the time a vote is taken for their vote to count. Action by a majority of the members present and voting shall constitute action by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All votes shall be recorded in writing by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in lieu of a meeting for the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may take an official action between regular meetings when the President, the Board, or the Executive Committee determines such action is necessary and that calling a special meeting is not feasible or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed action shall be presented in writing and a time limit for voting specified; voting shall take place as prescribed in the writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall consist of the President, the President-Elect, the Immediate Past President, and four additional Board members annually appointed by the President and approved by the Board of Governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee meeting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall meet at the call of the President, or upon call of the Secretary upon written application of three members of the Committee, upon one day's notice. Five members shall constitute a quorum. Action by a majority of members present and voting shall constitute action by the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may, subject to the President’s discretion, participate electronically in an in-person meeting. The President shall preside over meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee minutes and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes of each meeting of the Executive Committee shall be taken and distributed to the members of the Board of Governors within a reasonable period following such meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes of the Committee shall be part of the permanent records of the Board of Governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee powers, duties, and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee may exercise all the powers and perform all the duties of the Board of Governors between meetings of the Board, but only to the extent that action taken is not contrary to instructions of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee shall not amend the Bylaws, make rules or regulations governing nominations or elections, or initiate the taking of any referendum or poll of members of the Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers of the Bar (list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The officers of the Bar shall be a President, a President-Elect, a Secretary, and a Treasurer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Active members of the Bar shall serve as officers of the Bar.
